clinicalPearls: A mechanical (non-immune) haemolysis in which red cells are fragmented as they pass through abnormal small vessels
The blood film hallmark is schistocytes (red cell fragments) with features of haemolysis and often thrombocytopenia
The direct antiglobulin test is negative, distinguishing it from immune haemolysis
It is a syndrome, not a single disease, and the key task is to identify the underlying cause
Thrombotic microangiopathies (TTP, haemolytic uraemic syndrome) are urgent causes requiring specific treatment
Other causes include disseminated intravascular coagulation, malignant hypertension, pre-eclampsia/HELLP, disseminated cancer and mechanical heart valves
reference.pathophysiology: Microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia results from physical shearing of red cells within the microcirculation or across abnormal surfaces. In thrombotic microangiopathies, platelet-rich or fibrin thrombi partially occlude small vessels, and red cells passing through are fragmented into schistocytes. Similar fragmentation occurs across fibrin strands in disseminated intravascular coagulation, in vessels damaged by malignant hypertension or vasculitis, or across prosthetic valves. Because the process is mechanical, the antiglobulin test is negative, and consumption of platelets is common in thrombotic causes.
additionalDifferentials: Disseminated malignancy or mechanical valve haemolysis
additionalInvestigations: Blood film for schistocytes and platelet count
Coagulation screen and fibrinogen to assess for DIC
Cause-specific tests (ADAMTS13, complement studies, pregnancy assessment)
redFlags: Thrombocytopenia with neurological or renal features suggesting a thrombotic microangiopathy
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends entirely on the cause; thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is rapidly fatal untreated but responds to prompt plasma exchange, whereas other causes require treatment of the underlying process.
pitfalls: Missing thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, a medical emergency, by delaying ADAMTS13 testing and plasma exchange
Attributing MAHA to immune haemolysis despite a negative antiglobulin test
Failing to search systematically for the underlying cause
